http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/03/trump.text: Iran's foreign ministry said on Monday there were currently no negotiations with the United States but talks were under way with Oman over the management of the Strait of Hormuz."We are not currently negotiating with the United States. Our negotiations are with Oman to secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz," said foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei during a weekly press briefing.That statement contradicts US President Donald Trump who said that new negotiations with Iran would begin on Monday after he decided to hold off on striking the Islamic republic to pursue a deal to end the war entering its sixth month.Trump told reporters on Sunday that the talks would cover the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy supplies that has become a sticking point in the conflict, and the denuclearisation of Iran.For its part, Iran said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the strait, where a tanker reported an explosion nearby on Sunday, underscoring the continued volatility of the strategic waterway.Oil prices fell on Monday at the opening of Asian trade after Trump announced the new negotiations, with West Texas Intermediate dropping 4.7% to $80.72 (€69.99) per barrel.Washington and Tehran have been at war since 28 February, when the US and Israel launched surprise strikes against Iran, though months of on-off diplomacy have led to periods of relative calm.Following a return to strikes last month, fears had mounted that the fighting could escalate once again. Trump had threatened to hit Iran "very hard" and was reportedly considering renewed attacks including against energy infrastructure, with US embassies across the region on alert.Trump pulled back from that threat on Saturday, saying the "perimeters" of a deal were there."Now what we're doing is we're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon," Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday, without providing details of the venue or participants in the talks.The US president said he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on the strikes, which he claimed would have been "the biggest attack since World War II."Iranian media denied that Tehran had asked Trump not to strike.A previous ceasefire deal that included the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz fell through and Iran has since tightened its control over the waterway.The US president said at the start of the conflict that the war was necessary to deal with Iran's nuclear programme. Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Tehran insists the programme is entirely civilian in nature.'Exchange of views'Iranian lawmaker Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesman for the parliament's national security commission, said on Sunday that mediators were trying to revive the US-Iran memorandum of understanding that was agreed in June.That agreement was not intended as a final peace deal, but as a stepping stone to negotiations on a comprehensive agreement, though it did include provisions on Hormuz."They know that the main issue and, in fact, the key to the matter right now is the issue of the Strait of Hormuz, so yes, there is an exchange of views," Ghashghavi said.Posting on X, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said: "We must strive to compel the enemy to remain committed to what it has signed."Deal with Oman?Before the war, there was free passage for all vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, but Iran closed the strait during the war and now insists on retaining control and charging tolls, something the US rejects.That dispute sparked the return to strikes last month, as Tehran refused to let ships travel any route other than one which hugs the Iranian coast.On Sunday, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told state television that a deal was close with Oman, which sits on the other side of the strait, over a new route through it."We are now going to reach an understanding on a route acceptable to both sides, neither the northern route nor the southern route, but one that respects the sovereign rights of both sides and safeguards our national interests and security," he said.He insisted though that such an agreement did not mean the reopening of the strait.Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler said on Friday that traffic through Hormuz had dropped sharply.On Sunday, a tanker off the coast of Oman reported hearing an explosion near the vessel, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Centre reported, adding that the vessel and crew were all safe.

https://www.dw.com/en/migrant-tunnels-in.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5ISMy Lithuanian authorities have discovered 12 border tunnels so far this year Image: Lithuania's State Border Guard Service Advertisement Migrants are taking a new route to enter the Baltic country Lithuania : underground tunnels. These could be yet another attempt by Belarus to foster political instability, experts say. The country's border guards say they have found 12 such tunnels since the beginning of the year near the Belarusian border, with a length of up to 25 meters on the Lithuanian side. They are expecting more to emerge. Lithuania's border with Belarus is about 700 kilometers long, around 550 kilometers of which are fenced. "We have a ground seismic system, which can detect easily when there's a high level of vibrations over a long period of time," General Rustamas Liubajevas, the commander of Lithuania's State Border Guard Service, explained to DW. "We then wait [outside a tunnel] for the final stage of the digging and when the migrants come out, we apprehend them," he said, adding that up to 40 migrants exiting such tunnels had been arrested. Last year Lithuania registered 1652 irregular border crossings Image: Lithuania's State Border Guard Service Lithuania's prosecutor's office confirmed to DW that a pre-trial investigation was under way concerning approximately 20 people suspected of illegally digging a tunnel. Possible charges also include people smuggling. Due to the investigation, no media visits are currently authorized at the sites. Liubajevas is surprised migrants would attempt a subterranean crossing. "It takes a lot of effort to dig a tunnel and the migrants are arrested almost immediately — at most, one small group gets through," he said. Is Minsk lending a hand? The elaborate nature of the tunnels has led him to believe the migrants aren't working alone. "They wouldn't be able to go through with this without logistical support from the Belarusian authorities, as they need a lot of material like wood to strengthen the tunnels' walls," he stressed, adding that Belarus seemingly wanted to "keep the level of tension at the border high." Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenkohas denied facilitating migration flows to neighboring states. Similar migrant tunnels were discovered in the past in neighboring Poland. Margarita Seselgyte, Director of the Institute of International Relations and Political Science at Vilnius University, seconded Liubajevas' view. "Belarus is watching its border very closely, and the country doesn't fit in the natural migration route of migrants from Afghanistan, Iran or Sri Lanka," she told DW, adding that Minsk had to at least have turned a blind eye to any digging activity taking place near the border. Some experts believe the Belarusian state is envouraging the building of tunnels across the border Image: Lithuania's State Border Guard Service Seselgyte thus sees the tunnels as "a hybrid attack to cause anxiety in our society." "There is no vacuum in the world of security. As Lithuania has been closing vulnerabilities and reinforcing its border fence, Belarus is now helping migrants pass beneath it," she said. A long-running issue at the eastern flank of Europe For her, Minsk is assisting its close ally Moscow . Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 partly from Belarus, where it amassed troops under the pretext of military drills. "Lithuania has been very vocal in terms of defense against Russia, both conventional and hybrid, on an EU and Nato level, and they want to silence that voice by causing chaos in our country," the political scientist said. "The main goal is probably to weaken support for Ukraine and disrupt European unity," she added. Linas Kojala, CEO of Vilnius-based think tank Geopolitics and Security Studies Center, noted that the tunnels were keeping the border force busy – even if only a few migrants got through. He described the tunnels as "just another phase of the attack of weaponized migration we've been facing since 2021." Most of the Lithuania-Belarus border is lined with fencing Image: Arnaud Dumontier/MAXPPP/IMAGO That's when tens of thousands of migrants crossed into Lithuania, Poland and Latvia from Belarus. The European Union called the events a "state-sponsored instrumentalization of migrants at the EU external border," organized by Lukashenko. "Latvia, Poland, Lithuania and other countries have since set up external borders and we've managed to bring down illegal migration to a minimum," Kojala told DW. Lithuania's border guards registered 1652 attempts to enter the country irregularly in 2025. But this number won't go down to zero unless Minsk deals with the problem on its side, according to Kojala. "And that's unlikely: Belarus is clearly trying to pose as many problems as possible." 'Migration has long been used as a strategic tool' Belarus would be far from the first country to use migration as a strategic tool, underlined Robert Gonzci, an analyst at the Migration Research Institute in the Hungarian capital of Budapest. "It's a relatively low-cost, low-risk way of exerting pressure on other countries, and since the 1950s, there've been numerous documented cases of governments creating or manipulating migration flows," he said to DW. He added that even the Assyrian empire – which collapsed in the seventh century BC – used migration to consolidate imperial control. Gonzci didn't rule out that autonomous smuggling networks might be behind the recently discovered tunnels, which Belarusian authorities don't fully control. He added that Belarus and Russia have used weaponized migration to "divert Western attention from Russia's broader strategic agenda and create instability along NATO's eastern flank by fueling political and social tensions within European countries." Poland's EU border: A threat to nature and people To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The states organizing such operations – often authoritarian regimes – enjoyed an inherent strategic advantage, Gonzci stressed. "The target is usually a democratic state facing a fundamental dilemma: They must protect their sovereignty by securing their borders while simultaneously upholding their legal obligations and humanitarian commitments," he said. Eastern countries 'showing resilience' But experts seem to agree that countries on the EU's eastern flank have been doing rather well in that respect. "There's increasing cooperation and coordination between the Nordic and Baltic States and Poland, as these countries are facing similar challenges. And the EU Frontex mission has been sending additional equipment," Seselgyte said. Lithuania is currently receiving technical support from neighboring countries. "We are testing Polish scanning equipment, through which we can identify empty spaces underground. If these tools work well, we'll buy and deploy them," explained Liubajevas. https://www.dw.com/en/heat-wave-threaten.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5HrGE French authorities worked to keep vacationers away around Bordeaux, banning holiday camps for children and for people with disabilities Image: Emma Da Silva/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement A forecast of an incoming heat wave across France and Spain this week is threatening to hamper firefighting efforts as some of Europe's worst wildfires in decades rage on. France's weather service forecast temperatures of up to 40 degrees Celsius (100 degrees Fahrenheit) from Tuesday, while Spain's AEMET warned of a new heat wave from Wednesday till the end of the week, with highs of 42 degree Celsius in the northeast and 39 degrees Celsius in central regions. Authorities said soaring temperatures, dry winds and low humidity would push wildfire danger to "extreme" levels, even as forests turned tinder-dry by successive heat waves this year. The return of searing temperatures, from Tuesday in France and from Wednesday in Spain, threaten to complicate fire-fighting efforts [FILE: July 23, 2026] Image: Julien De Rosa/AFP Thousands of firefighters and water-dropping aircraft raced to contain the blazes before temperatures rise further. Experts linked the scale of the fires to increasingly frequent and intense heat waves driven by climate change , as hotter and drier conditions are making wildfires more destructive. Macron warns of 'hard' times In France, President Emmanuel Macron said one fire in the Landes region had been contained, but a much larger wildfire near Bordeaux continued to burn after scorching about 42,000 hectares, forcing around 220,000 people to evacuate and destroying hundreds of homes. "The weeks ahead will be hard. We must hold firm," Macron said. Overnight on Tuesday, firefighters prevented a massive wildfire along the Atlantic coast west of Bordeaux from spreading, authorities said. According to officials, 93 firefighters have been injured since the operation began. Aid from Germany arrived in the region on Monday in the form of two transport helicopters and an A400M transport aircraft carrying equipment. In Spain, wildfires west of Madrid and in other regions have forced about 60,000 people to flee. With the coming heat wave threatening to fuel further spread of the wildfires, Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska firefighters in Spain made progress after a "positive night" against wildfires to the west of Madrid. Some 150,000 hectares of land have burned in Spain and 115,000 hectares in France since the start of this year. At a campsite near Navaluenga, west of the capital, ravaged by Spain's worst wildfire on record, the site co-owner Maria Angeles Canete said her family lost everything. "We had this campsite, we had another one, and we've lost it all. We have nothing," she told the AFP news agency. Has Europe lost control of its wildfires? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video EU firefighting resources stretched thin The European Union deployed additional firefighting aircraft to France, while EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib warned that resources are under growing strain as extreme fire conditions spread across southern and central Europe. "Extreme conditions are looming for Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, in addition to France, the Iberian Peninsula... where the situation is expected to worsen, including in Portugal starting today," Lahbib said. In Italy , a wildfire in the southern Puglia region forced the evacuation of hundreds of tourists from beaches and campgrounds, authorities said. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/c74emd.text: Orangutans in danger as wildfires blaze through Borneo Orangutans in danger as wildfires blaze through Borneo Close A weak orangutan was found laying on the ground in Ketapang, West Kalimantan on Borneo island. Indonesia has intensified efforts to contain haze from wildfires across six provinces in Borneo and Sumatra islands. The wildfires have destroyed part of the habitat of hundreds of orangutans and risking the survival of the species. "The situation is quite critical", said Karmele Llano Sanchez, CEO of the wildlife foundation Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI). Sanchez said the fires are "leaving [the orangutans] without any food or water". The orangutan found will be moved to a rehabilitation centre to get more treatment and will be released back into the wild after recovery, according to YIARI. https://nineoclock.ro/wolf-theiss-advise.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Wolf Theiss advised Nordic Tyre Group, a leading independent tyre distributor across the Nordic and Baltic markets, on its acquisition of 100% of the shares in Dinamic92 Distribution S.R.L., a Romanian wholesaler and distributor headquartered in Piatra Neamț. The transaction, which closed on 30 September 2026, marks the group’s entry into the Romanian market and represents its first acquisition since becoming part of Axcel’s portfolio in 2025. Wolf Theiss advised Nordic Tyre Group on the Romanian law aspects of the transaction, including assistance with due diligence, transaction structuring and the transfer of the entire share capital of Dinamic92 Distribution S.R.L. as well as coordination with the client and other advisors involved in the transaction. The Wolf Theiss team was led by Partner Ileana Glodeanu, supported by Senior Associate Delia Dumitrescu and Associates Vlad Catană and Laurenţiu Bolborici (all Corporate/M&A). The team further included Counsel Flavius Florea (Data Protection, IP & TMT), Partner Anca Jurcovan, Senior Associate Maria Popescu (both Competition & FDI), Partner Adelina Iftime-Blăgean, Counsel Andreea Stan (both Employment), Senior Associate Smaranda Văcaru (Banking & Finance), Counsel Dana Toma, Senior Associate Antonia Nica and Associate Sorana Grosu (all Real Estate & Construction) and Senior Associate Bogdan Lamatic (Litigation). “ Nordic Tyre Group’s entry into Romania with Dinamic92 represents a strategic expansion into Eastern Europe and marks the next growth chapter for the group. We appreciate the support of the Wolf Theiss throughout the signing and closing of our acquisition in Romania. Ileana and the entire team understood our objectives and helped bring the transaction to a successful close.” – Patrick Bergander, CEO, Nordic Tyre Group “It was a pleasure to support Nordic Tyre on this transaction and its entry into the Romanian market. We would like to thank all parties involved for their collaboration throughout the process, we are very happy to have contributed to the successful completion of this acquisition.” – Ileana Glodeanu, M&A Partner, Wolf Theiss Nordic Tyre Group is one of the leading independent tyre wholesale and distribution platforms in Europe, operating across the Nordics and Baltics, with annual revenue of approximately EUR 400 million. The group is backed by Nordic private equity firm Axcel and combines a strong supplier network, extensive logistics setup, and a unique, proprietary software platform to provide the broadest and most reliable tyre offering to its customers. Dinamic92 Distribution is the leading independent tyre wholesaler in Romania. Founded in 1992 by the Tofan family in Piatra Neamt, the company has grown over more than three decades into a trusted partner for tyre retailers and workshops across the country. Dinamic92 serves a wide range of customers, from independent workshops to national tyre retailers, through locations in Piatra Neamţ, Cluj-Napoca, Constanţa, Timişoara and Bucharest, with an annual distribution volume of approximately 700,000 tyres.
